proposal:
STATUS: nothing executed; hand derivations from the supplied code; literature (Heule-Kiesl-Biere PR clauses, Buss-Thapen SPR without new variables) cited from memory. No polynomial-SAT claim.

A. AUDIT (code-level)
1. Size. The k-pair quotient has m=2^(k+1)+k^2 clauses; the measured peak 8=2^(k-1) at k=4 is below m/4. Neon58 shows no state growth beyond input size. Its measured cost is per-state IALH work, so I target work, not peak.
2. In `refute`, modulus-0 rows with a single nonzero coefficient (x=c on every UP-surviving tuple) are sound units, i.e. failed-literal facts already paid for. When no dual exists they are discarded; `elim_plus(reduced)` never sees them.
3. `windows` keeps `ordered[:max_windows]` by (size, lexicographic IDs), so refutation power depends on numbering. The fixture's decisive window is, by my count, 240th of 290 with 256 kept.
4. `_verify_certificate` tests `r*r*n+work` after running the r^2 parity loop: sound, but not a pre-spend budget.
5. I found no soundness defect in block coverage: blocks are built from every original clause.

B. RULE DU (dominance unit): sound, restricted
Let l, m be literals on distinct variables. l is dominated by m in F if every D in F with (not l) and m both absent has some E in F with l not in E and E minus {not l} contained in D minus {l, not m}.
Lemma. If t satisfies F and t(l)=1, then t[l:=0, m:=1] satisfies F. Hence F and F+(not l) are equisatisfiable, and every model of F+(not l) is a model of F.
Proof. Clauses containing (not l) or m hold after the change. Otherwise E minus {not l} mentions neither variable, t satisfies it because t falsifies (not l), and it lies inside D. QED.
This is a subset-checked special case of SPR with a two-literal witness; it is not new as logic. Units must be added one at a time and re-checked against the enlarged formula. For F={(1 2)} both (-1) and (-2) pass individually; after adding (-1), the test for (-2) fails on clause (-1), as it must.
Certificate: (l, m) plus one subsumer index per affected clause. Checking is subset tests, O(N) bit operations per unit, with no truth tables and no search. Equivalence is lost, so receipts must say equisatisfiable; SAT models transfer unchanged.

C. NEON58
Inferred pinned quotient numbering (consistent with the trusted reorder): twins (v, v+8), side A odd, side B even. For l=v+8, m=v: every positive clause contains m, and each negative D containing -v has E equal to D with -v replaced by -(v+8). Eight sequential units -9..-16 pass. Propagation leaves 8 variables and 18 clauses: the sixteen binaries (a or b), plus (-1 -3 -5 -7) and (-2 -4 -6 -8). Any a=0 unit-propagates every b=1 and falsifies the B clause, so the table on window (1,3,5,7) is empty: root refutation, no branching.
Composition order: BLQ first (XOR-gadget pairs are literals only in the quotient), then DU, then residual. On the original 20-variable input only -9, -10, -11, -12 are DU-valid.
k-family prediction (unimplemented): 2k units, residual k^2+2 clauses. For k<=5 the pinned window exists. For k>5 the negative clause exceeds IALH width, and item A2 (promote x=1 rows to units) is needed for a root refutation.

D. EXTRAS
DU is one-directional. An extra clause is harmless iff it contains m, contains (not l), avoids both variables, or has a subsumer. The fixture's extras (1 -12) and (3 5 -16) destroy the twin/OR-module property of five pairs yet keep all eight units valid. An extra (-1 6) kills pair (1,9) in both directions.

E. TOTAL WORK
Hash-based discovery (E=R or R+{not l}) costs O(n * sum|D|^2) word operations per pass, with at most n passes: O(n^2 * w * N) bits, crudely O(N^4). No quadratic claim. Checking costs O(nN). Residual work is unchanged in the worst case.

F. WHAT IT CANNOT DO
Pigeonhole (h>=2) has no dominated literal (hand check): a positive literal needs m in the same pigeon clause, which exposes hole clauses with no subsumer; a negative literal meets h hole clauses and one m satisfies only one. To my recollection PHP has short SPR refutations with four-variable swap witnesses, but those are conditional binary clauses, and deciding witness existence is NP-hard in general. Brute-forcing bounded witnesses is polynomial with exponent at least 6 and has no completeness proof. I expect random 3-CNF, Tseitin after BLQ and the ordering principle to be DU-irreducible (unchecked). DU is a restricted preprocessing class, not a SAT algorithm.

INDEPENDENT TESTS
(i) Strip the eight unit clauses from the fixture: a DU checker must accept -9..-16 sequentially, and an exact twin/OR-module test must reject pairs (1,9), (3,11), (5,13), (4,12), (8,16).
(ii) Batch acceptance on {(1 2)} must be rejected.
(iii) PHP h=2..5: zero DU candidates.
(iv) Fixture receipt, by hand count: compression skipped `all_variables_in_odd_blocks`; core `no_clauses_removed`; root `empty_table` at window [1,3,5,7]; windows=240, tuples=1792.
missing_theorem:
MT1 (small, Lean-ready). The DU lemma and its sequential composition: a chain F=F0, F1, ..., Ft, each adding one DU unit checked against its predecessor, gives F SAT iff Ft SAT. Compose with BLQ equivalence and the UNSAT-only core.

MT2 (real gap: order-independence). DU is not confluent as rewriting: for twins, either unit blocks the other. Needed: if some DU sequence followed by unit propagation and single-literal failed-literal closure derives the empty clause, then every maximal greedy DU sequence does. I have neither a proof nor a counterexample. An exhaustive test over all CNFs on at most 5 variables with at most 8 clauses, over all orders, would falsify it cheaply. Without MT2, greedy discovery has no completeness statement even inside the DU class.

MT3 (the obstruction for arbitrary CNF). A polynomial bound on finding width-s SPR clauses with witnesses of support at most t that, with UP closure, refute every formula having such a refutation of polynomial length. Bounding (s,t) makes each candidate check polynomial, but each added clause can invalidate later candidates, so the sequence search is unbounded. No lower bound is claimed and I know no upper bound. Nothing here bounds residual work on DU-irreducible inputs.
self_attack:
1. Not novel as logic. The contribution is the subset-only certificate, the cost accounting, placement after BLQ, the one-sided-extras characterisation and the audit items.
2. Neon58 was never superpolynomial in encoded size; DU removes a factor on one family.
3. The fixture is the rule's output, not its discovery. A match shows only that pinned v5 root-refutes the post-DU formula. I do not predict pinned v5 on the stripped formula with extras.
4. Hand-trace risks. The quotient numbering is inferred. The window count (228 below size 4, quad twelfth of size 4) could be wrong; if it is off by 17 the window is truncated and the peak prediction may fail. I assume single-tuple tables pass through `hull_rows` with zero-column matrices, as they must already do after any unit.
5. Equisatisfiability weakens the pipeline's exact-equivalence receipts. Any step assuming model-set preservation must not consume DU output as equivalent, and the core subset check must be against F plus certified units.
6. A batched implementation is unsound.
7. MT2 may be false. Then greedy needs backtracking and the O(N^4) bound covers one sequence only.
8. PHP and SPR statements are from memory. A2 units add canon work per node; unmeasured. The irreducibility expectations in F are unchecked beyond PHP.
mechanism_signature: Sequential dominance units (DU): literal l is dominated by m when every clause of F restricted by {l=0, m=1} is subsumed by a clause of F restricted by {l=1}; add unit (not l). Satisfiability-preserving, not equivalence-preserving. Certificate is (l, m, subsumer index per affected clause), checked by subset tests only. Runs after the BLQ quotient and before IALH. Companion: promote single-variable IALH equality rows to units.
delta_from_prior: Round 89 (BVA), round 90 (bound-set quotient) and Fable73 (twin contraction) add variables or rewrite clauses and need the exact symmetric OR-module. Round 91 was a branching rule. DU adds no variable and rewrites nothing: it appends certified units, needs dominance in one direction only, and so survives one-sided extras where twin contraction fails (five of eight pairs in the fixture). Also new: equality rows discarded by `refute` (A2), numbering-dependent window truncation (A3), the batch-unsoundness trap, the hand check that pigeonhole has no dominated literal, and the remark that Neon58's peak is below its clause count.
